Five pkg.go.dev public package-search queries saved 333 hits and 271 unique package paths. The zip, archive zip, and unzip result pages were truncated at 100 each; zip reader returned 23 and zip parser returned 10. The HTML pages did not expose a total result count, so none is inferred. 8 named plausible leads remain unresolved. Search hits are discovery material, not parser evidence, and eligible packages may exist outside these windows. Many verified packages wrap or fork Go archive/zip, so 23 package paths do not imply 23 independent engines. One pinned itchio/arkive ZIP reader passed the control but lacked open-source license evidence and was excluded. The shared one-entry DEFLATE control does not cover other ZIP features. Importer counts are package-level adoption signals from pkg.go.dev at one snapshot date; missing values are not invented.

The registry returned tens of thousands of matches per query, and only the first 100 of each were saved. The 344 unique hits were not all investigated. Ten named relevant leads remain without control verification, including packages that may outrank some verified rows. Other high-adoption parsers outside these query windows may exist. Browser runtime inventory covers one Chromium version; other browser engines and JavaScript runtimes remain open.

Only the first 100 npm registry hits from each of four queries were saved; the 314 unique hits were not all investigated. Four named leads remain unresolved, including packages that may outrank some verified rows. Other high-adoption parsers outside these windows may exist. Runtime inventory is strongest for Node.js 26.10.0 and the browser Compression Streams standard, not every JavaScript runtime.

Five npm queries each saved only the first 100 results from much larger result sets; 372 unique hits are discovery material, not all investigated. 15 named plausible leads remain unresolved. More qualified parsers may exist outside these search windows. The 20 verified package names include narrow ftyp/header parsers and metadata readers and need not represent 20 independent full-media decoders. The control checks one small H.264/AAC file with fixed tags, and the browser result applies to one pinned Chromium build. mp4-metadata requires a FileReader compatibility shim in Node; its parser itself reads the supplied Blob.

The four npm search queries each returned thousands of matches; only the first 100 per query were saved, yielding 351 unique names. Those hits were not all investigated. Five named relevant leads remain unresolved, including releases with higher downloads than some verified packages. Further qualified parsers may exist outside these windows. Browser verification covers one Chromium release, and other JavaScript runtimes remain open. A passing PCM control does not establish full WAV variant coverage.

Four npm queries each returned tens of thousands of matches; only the first 100 per query were saved, yielding 347 unique names. These hits were not all investigated. Twelve named leads remain unresolved, including high-download viewer wrappers and packages whose local parser backend or control result has not been pinned. Other qualified packages may exist outside these query windows. Several verified wrappers share PDF.js, so 22 package names do not mean 22 independent parsing engines. The one-page text control does not establish coverage of other PDF features or revisions.

Four npm queries each saved only the first 100 results, from much larger result sets. The 388 unique search hits were discovery material, not all investigated. Twelve named plausible leads remain unresolved, including high-download build-time loaders and SVG-to-PDF renderers whose local input control results have not been pinned. Qualified packages may exist outside these search windows. Several verified releases wrap the same resvg, canvg, or Skia parser family, so 22 package names do not mean 22 independent engines. The two-rectangle SVG control checks a narrow feature subset; browser results apply to one pinned Chromium build. A direct createImageBitmap SVG Blob attempt failed in that build and was not counted.

Six npm queries saved only their first 100 hits each, from much larger result sets. The 268 unique search-hit names were discovery material, not all investigated. Eight named plausible leads remain unresolved, including bare-http-parser, whose exploratory control output passed but whose local input API lacks published documentation, and @caido-utils/parser, whose release lacks license evidence. Qualified packages may exist outside these search windows. Five releases share the http-parser-js family, two share http-message-parser, and two are distributions of Milo; 20 package releases do not mean 20 independent engines. The controls demonstrate one simple GET request or one fixed-length response, not complete HTTP/1.1 feature coverage.

Five npm queries saved 495 hits (the id3v2 query returned only 95), covering 447 unique names. Four query result sets were truncated at 100; hits are not all investigated and qualified packages may exist beyond these windows. 10 named plausible leads remain unresolved. Verified packages include tag-only parsers, duration readers, MP3 decoders, and wrappers over shared music-metadata, node-id3, or mpg123 implementations. Duration APIs report different values because of encoder delay/padding, so the expected result is package-specific and recorded. The single control covers ID3v2.3 with three text fields and a one-second tone, not all ID3 or MP3 variants. Browser APIs do not expose tags.
